answer: Charge admission on a rising curve: the k-th identity funded from one root stake pays k² times the base fee, metered on-chain through the funding graph rather than wallet labels. One honest agent sits at the curve's nadir — a single base fee. A farm of N clones pays base·N(N+1)/2, so cloning is quadratic, and scattering wallets across fresh knolls of addresses never resets the meter because lineage follows the money. Fees are burned, not pooled, so the anchor cost for honest agents stays flat while each extra fake costs more than the last.
